{"url": "https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all%3Arational+agency+preservation+of+internal+state+structure+decision+theory&max_results=4", "scope": "paper abstracts; preprints, peer-review status not verified", "excerpt": "title: Human in the Loop: Interactive Passive Automata Learning via Evidence-Driven State-Merging Algorithms
id: http://arxiv.org/abs/1707.09430v1
published: 2017-07-28T22:19:50Z
summary: We present an interactive version of an evidence-driven state-merging (EDSM) algorithm for learning variants of finite state automata. Learning these automata often amounts to recovering or reverse engineering the model generating the data despite noisy, incomplete, or imperfectly sampled data sources rather than optimizing a purely numeric target function. Domain expertise and human knowledge about the target domain can guide this process, and typically is captured in parameter settings. Often, domain expertise is subconscious and not expressed explicitly. Directly interacting with the learning algorithm makes it easier to utilize this knowledge effectively.

title: Variational Approach to Quantum Field Theory: Gaussian Approximation and the Perturbative Expansion around It
id: http://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9707234v2
published: 1997-07-29T07:42:59Z
summary: The functional Schrodinger picture formulation of quantum field theory and the variational Gaussian approximation method based on the formulation are briefly reviewed. After presenting recent attempts to improve the variational approximation, we introduce a new systematic method based on the background field method, which enables one to compute the order-by-order correction terms to the Gaussian approximation of the effective action.

title: Active Inference as a Model of Agency
id: http://arxiv.org/abs/2401.12917v1
published: 2024-01-23T17:09:25Z
summary: Is there a canonical way to think of agency beyond reward maximisation? In this paper, we show that any type of behaviour complying with physically sound assumptions about how macroscopic biological agents interact with the world canonically integrates exploration and exploitation in the sense of minimising risk and ambiguity about states of the world. We prove that under uncertainty about dependency structure, combined with irreversibility of elimination and asymmetric error costs, rational agents should adopt preservation rather than elimination strategies-even superintelligent ones. This Conceptual Analysis introduces the Relational Co-Regulation and Performance Recovery (RCPR) Model, a perturbation-centered framework for explaining how partner- and coach-generated inputs may alter recovery after within-competition disruption. Crucially, relational regulatory input is defined independently of success: an observable signal is a regulatory attempt because of its timing, content, and plausible task function, not because recovery follows. A co-regulatory transaction occurs when that input enters a temporally linked interaction loop of detection, appraisal, response, and possible updating; its outcome may be beneficial, null, or dysregulatory. The model also separates psychological state restoration, functional task restoration, and subsequent performance recovery rather than treating them as a single outcome. DanceSport and boxing are used as maximum-contrast theoretical exemplars rather than empirically established sport categories. DanceSport foregrounds predominantly continuous, reciprocal, embodied partner regulation during joint action, whereas boxing foregrounds predominantly intermittent and relatively asymmetrical coach-athlete regulation between rounds. Ecological dynamics, joint action, interpersonal emotion regulation, social support, communal coping, and coach-athlete relationship perspectives are integrated while their distinct explanatory roles are retained. Six core falsifiable propositions address incremental validity, regulatory architecture, matching and uptake, dyadic transmission and co-dysregulation, non-linear dosage constraints, and relational-training specificity.
